content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am experiencing the same issue as described. My laptop's IP is 192.168.100.100, [product_name] device is at 192.168.100.11, and the [product_name] operator panel is at 192.168.100.51. All devices are on subnet 255.255.255.0 with a gateway of 192.168.100.1. I am using [product_name] engineering software [version_no]. When I do not add a [product_name] device in the network project and go online, the devices are detected automatically, including the operator panel. However, when attempting to download, I receive an error: 'unable to access the remote device.'
Are you using a USB to Ethernet converter? Is 192.168.100.100 the IP address for this converter?
That's right. I suspected the USB adapter might be causing the problem, so I also tried connecting via the laptop's built-in Ethernet port, but the issue persisted.

The issue has been resolved. Installing [product_name] engineering software [version_no] fixed the problem. It appears the newly purchased [product_name] device has firmware supported only by this newer software version.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced download failures when connecting to [product_name] devices using an older version of [product_name] engineering software, caused by a compatibility issue between the software version and newer device firmware. Updating the software resolved the access problem and enabled successful communication.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects seamless program downloads to [product_name] devices and operator panels, without access errors, regardless of hardware or firmware versions.
